title: Exact Confidence Radius for Difference in Means with Bounded Outcomes under Complete Randomization
banked_reason: D0.5 graded incremental below the field floor; paper score ceiling 5.6 < 7.4, with no bounded in-scope repair to field tier.
gap_reasons: under the bar; no bounded fix in scope
the nine-row theorem is not reproducible from the article itself because its load-bearing cell-cover DAGs are private
four exact conventional-level radii and five unresolved brackets
proof_attempt_summary: The D-stage derived an exact variational formulation, all-threshold sharp-null equivalence, a finite MILP formulation, a convex sandwich, analytic regimes, and binary-calibration counterexamples. D0.5 judged the delivered package incremental below the required field floor, with a 5.6 paper-score ceiling against 7.4; five radii remain bracketed rather than exact, and the finite records supporting the nine-row upper bounds are not public artifacts in this bank. A future re-raise needs declared, independently checkable certificate records and a broader result than the current fixed-center table, plus theorem-level comparison with the closest literature.
tldr: For fixed potential outcomes taking values in \([0,1]\) under complete randomization, the paper gives an exact variational characterization, and an equivalent finite MILP characterization, of the smallest deterministic symmetric radius around ordinary difference in means. Every worst-case tail probability is already attained within the sharp-null subclass. Numerical evaluation is separate: proved hypergeometric/convex certificates and exact rational cell-cover certificates give only nine stated conventional-level results, four exact radii and five brackets narrower than \(1/100\). Fractional sharp-null populations show that binary-only calibration can undercover. No general scalable solver, balanced-\(n=20\) precision, or unrestricted \(n=30\) radius is claimed.
gap: Finite-sample bounded-outcome work supplies concentration radii, variance-adaptive intervals, or binary-outcome test inversion. Convex-order work supplies hypergeometric comparisons for convex functionals. None of the inspected sources identifies the exact strict two-sided assignment rank of ordinary difference in means over every bounded-real schedule or certifies the nine specified finite designs.
fill: The project proves the centered-sum minimax formula, develops the binary-lower and convex-upper rank certificate and its equality frontier, derives the supported analytic regimes, and supplies replayable exact cell-cover proofs for the nine stated brackets. The unresolved five exact values are isolated as a construction question rather than hidden behind numerical output.
